This is further supported by the presence of marked, thick-rimmed contrast enhancement and central necrosis, which are classic features of IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. The tumor also has relatively sharp boundaries (thin transition zone), which is more typical of IDH-wildtype gliomas than the diffusely infiltrative IDH-mutant astrocytomas. Finally, the absence of a T2-FLAIR mismatch sign argues against an IDH-mutant astrocytoma. There are no significant features to suggest an IDH-mutant tumor.

The tumor also crosses the midline through the corpus callosum, another feature often associated with glioblastoma. While the total tumor volume is relatively small and there is no significant midline shift, these factors are insufficient to outweigh the definitive high-grade features of necrosis and ring-enhancement.

overall_comment: The patient is a 46-year-old male with a solitary, deep midline tumor involving the bilateral thalami, brainstem, and corpus callosum. MRI features of marked, thick-rimmed contrast enhancement and central necrosis are definitive for a high-grade glioma. These features, combined with the midline location and sharply defined borders, are highly characteristic of a Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4.
